**Intake review** — fleet monitor, 2026-10-29

- **Related:** design #2065 (refundable grants), design PR #2293 (§3 is the source of both decisions). Already in the `user/review` lane.
- **Still live:** no decision recorded on the issue yet; the build issues read the answer from config, so nothing has defaulted it in code as of this run.
- **Notes:** an `## Acceptance criteria` section was appended (decisions recorded + reflected as config defaults). This is a decision only Drew can make; per the house rule the substance is: **Decision 1** — how long a Steam-key grant stays pending before it vests: A. 14 days (design recommendation; closes essentially all refund exposure, users wait up to 14 days), B. 48 hours (2-day wait, leaves a 12-day exposure hole), C. 14 days with early vest on evidence (needs a trustworthy signal Steam doesn't reliably expose), D. none (status quo #2065 replaces). **Decision 2** — whether pending tokens are spendable; design recommends not spendable at all. Recommendation on the issue: A + not spendable. A one-line answer closes it.
- **Risks:** none in deciding; the risk is NOT deciding and having a build issue default it silently.
- **Suggested approach:** Drew rules here; the monitor has set priority/high + effort/xs to reflect that it's a one-line decision blocking a design's implementation.
- Labels normalized: kind/question, source/human, priority/high, effort/xs, meta/enriched (user/review retained).

# Drew's ruling on the grant terms — recorded 2026-11-08

Drew ruled on these terms on 2026-11-08 07:14 CST, as question 5 of the #2043 policy set. His words, verbatim:

> 1 yes, units and pending units and revoked units 3 currencies 2 finite except transfers from the account for supplying currency, named like tiger beetle would be. 3 yes 4 yes 5 yes except allow trading pending units if both parties accept/sign. transfer cancel option that originator can trade their pending units 1:1 for revoked units not after (14 days from Init) which also attaches the notBefore trade from pending units to units. only trade able as a chained item from initial grant by us. any pending units without a provided option contract will be denied by us to trade in, our clients will require it as an input for any pending unit trade. at 28 days notAfter signature is enabled, we automatically sign and put the transfer at 14 days and each users contracted other users can redeem against that users account using their signed chained contract, they can oresubmit signs counterdigned contracts to us and we will run as soon as all the chains up to them are done. maybe our clients require all such contracts are submitted to us by pending unit owner and then other party ckuntersigns only transactions escrowed to us with all chains up to original also escrowed so they can know they'll either get units or rejected units as we process entire batch atomically?

## Base terms — ACCEPTED as recommended

Decision 1 and Decision 2 are this issue's own; the remaining three are the #2043 design §8 Q5 recommendations, accepted in the same ruling:

- Decision 1 (window length): **A — 14 days** (Steam-direct hold).
- Decision 2: pending units never spendable (as spending) — but see the amendment below.
- Per-processor / per-source chargeback horizon.
- Debt never silently expires (write-off only signed/public).
- For-cause-only revocation for first-party premium.

## Amendment — pending-unit trading (NEW mechanism, not in the current design)

Drew adds: **allow trading pending units if both parties accept/sign.** As recorded from his text:

1. **Cancel option:** the originator can trade their pending units 1:1 for revoked units, not after 14 days from Init; exercising it also attaches the notBefore trade from pending units to units.
2. **Chained only:** pending units are tradable only as a chained item from the initial grant by us.
3. **Contract required:** any pending units without a provided option contract will be denied by us to trade in; our clients will require the option contract as an input for any pending-unit trade.
4. **At 28 days:** the notAfter signature is enabled; we automatically sign and put the transfer at 14 days. (His text; see UNRESOLVED below.)
5. **Chained redemption:** each user's contracted other users can redeem against that user's account using their signed chained contract; they can resubmit signed countersigned contracts to us and we will run them as soon as all the chains up to them are done. (His "oresubmit signs" is recorded verbatim in the quote above; the reading "resubmit signed" is a transcription guess, not a ruling.)

## PROPOSAL — not a hard ruling (his sentence ends with "?"; he is thinking it through)

The final sentence of his ruling — clients requiring all such contracts to be submitted by the pending-unit owner, the other party countersigning only transactions escrowed to us with all chains up to the original also escrowed, so participants know they will either get units or rejected units as we process the entire batch atomically — is recorded as an **open proposal**, not a decision. ("ckuntersigns" = countersigns, transcription reading.)

## UNRESOLVED — needs Drew's confirmation before this is design

- "Init" — the start point the 14-day cancel window runs from (presumably the initial grant; not stated).
- "which also attaches the notBefore trade from pending units to units" — what exactly is attached, and to what.
- "we automatically sign and put the transfer at 14 days" — 14 days measured from what, effective when.
- "rejected units" in the escrow proposal vs "revoked units" in the cancel option — same thing or different?
- How trading interacts with Decision 2's "pending not spendable, at all": this amendment makes pending units transferable between consenting parties while keeping them unspendable on services; Decision 2's acceptance line needs rewording to match.

## Acceptance-criteria note

Decision 1 = A (14 days) is now recorded, chooser: Drew. Decision 2 is recorded as MODIFIED by the amendment above (unspendable; tradable only under chained option contracts). This issue stays open: the trading mechanism is not yet designed, and the config defaults the #2065 build issues read need to reflect the base terms and the amendment once the UNRESOLVED points are confirmed.
